summary: digital-r6-request-table-01 and digital-r6-important-policy PDFs acquired via plain fetch and SHA-256-locked in sources/source-lock.json, per ADR-009 (source identity = binary hash, not URL).
Deterministic page-aware PDF extraction (scripts/pdf-extraction) added, providing pdfjs-dist-based glyph/text/coordinate extraction later reused by the pdfjs-baseline document-understanding adapter.

Document Understanding Benchmark layer created; case-001 defined (target row: item 020 / expense 01-95, PDF page index 11) with Ground Truth frozen by manual visual verification against the locked PDF binary; pdfjs-baseline and pymupdf-baseline adapters registered.

First benchmark run: pdfjs-baseline 8/11, pymupdf-baseline 8/11 under the then-current check set (including raw_delta_glyph_preserved). item_name_exact_match FAILed (header-row hierarchy ambiguity, but the correct row was present among candidates); unit_exact_match FAILed (label absent on target page); expense_name_exact_match_after_line_join FAILed (an unrelated annotation column contaminated the reconstructed wrapped label).

Docling adapter integrated with a dedicated normalizer (normalize-docling.mjs) that preserves native table-cell structure rather than flattening it; added closeCjkWrapSpaces (CJK wrap-space closing) and reconstructNumericToken (numeric comma-group reversal correction) rules, both verified across multiple independent cells on this page.

Docling scored 9/11 vs. pdfjs/pymupdf's 8/11: Docling's table-cell separation resolved expense_name_exact_match_after_line_join, the two-column conflation that broke both flat-text baselines. Header-row hierarchy ambiguity and target-page unit-label absence remained unresolved for Docling too.

PR review found raw_delta_glyph_preserved's name/description overstated what was measured — for Docling, deltaRaw could be a normalizer-constructed concatenation of two separate raw cells, not a literal single raw token. Renamed to delta_glyph_observed_and_associated with corrected note language distinguishing 'genuinely present in engine output' from 'literal raw token'.
Document Understanding Benchmark research checkpoint merged to main via PR #1.

delta_glyph_observed_and_associated (hardcoded expected: 'contains △' regardless of Ground Truth) replaced with delta_sign_evidence_matches_source, which derives the expected glyph state from Ground Truth's own deltaRaw field. Discovered via case-002's out-of-sample run, whose correctly glyph-free Ground Truth could never have passed the old hardcoded check.

case-001 re-scored under the corrected evaluator: pdfjs-baseline 8/11, pymupdf-baseline 8/11, docling 9/11 — unchanged, since case-001's Ground Truth deltaRaw genuinely carries a △ glyph and every engine's own output genuinely contained one.

Header-row hierarchy ambiguity (multiple NNN <name>-shaped rows at different 項/目 levels) is unresolved for all three engines; item_name_exact_match cannot resolve to a single row without an indentation/hierarchy-level detection mechanism not yet built.
Docling produced no cell for case-001's target row's request-number column (requestNo recovered as null) — an unresolved per-engine limitation, not yet investigated.

A general per-page/document-level unit-label lookup is unimplemented; unit_exact_match correctly fails for all three engines because the '千円' label lives only on an earlier summary page, not on case-001's target page.
